lit_intro: Each member reviewed at least one source. Each paragraph states the problem, the method and the key finding, and how the source relates to our results.
lit: Gulluoglu et al. (2026), the course paper, asks whether current AI tools can turn the molecule drawings in real journal PDFs into SMILES, a task that published benchmarks avoid by testing single, cleanly cropped images. The authors hand-curated an answer key for six open-access 2026 papers (222 drawn molecules; 220 unique structures after canonicalization, the count our scorer uses) and scored every system by exact match of canonical SMILES. Existing readers run on Docling's figure images found almost nothing (DECIMER and MolVec none, MolScribe one molecule), because they read plots, tables and text as molecules and cannot combine a scaffold with its R-group table. A Claude Code pipeline (Docling figures, a molecule gate, MolScribe, RDKit) found 13 molecules, and ChatGPT-5.5 output 5,329 SMILES to find 32. The authors conclude that figure segmentation, not recognition, is the bottleneck. Our results support that and show what comes next. With the same MolScribe reader, our pipeline on MolDetV2 crops found 54 molecules instead of 13, so better segmentation was the first gain. The molecules still missed are mostly scaffold-plus-R-group structures in papers 2, 4 and 19, which no reader can produce from a single crop.
